I've been working this land for 45 years — I know what it needs. Quzhou soil is deep loam, and the well gives me water when the rains don't come, which is most summers. My son is in the city, so I manage most of the field work myself or with my husband. I can't do heavy labor the way I used to.

I'll put 5 mu in maize and 4 mu in cotton. Maize is easier on my body — one planting, mostly machine work for the village co-op, and a decent price. Cotton I keep because I know it, and in a good year it pays better per mu. But I won't expand it because picking is brutal alone.

I buy hybrid seeds from the township supply station — same place I've gone for twenty years. For maize I use whichever hybrid the station recommends this season; they know what does well locally. For cotton I use Bt hybrid, which cut my spraying down considerably ten years ago and I've stuck with it.

Fertilizer: I put down compound fertilizer before planting, then top-dress urea on the maize when it's knee-high. Cotton gets more potassium — I learned that the hard way when bolls were small. I pump the well four times each crop: once before sowing, once at key growth stage, once at flowering, once if July turns dry. I spray maize twice — once for borers, once if leaf blight appears. Cotton still needs more spraying than maize even with Bt, mostly for aphids and spider mites in August.

I plough with rotary tiller each spring — the soil needs loosening and it buries last year's stalks.
